Paying From Abroad

Sending rent from outside the UK

Use the IBAN and SWIFT/BIC above. Please send in pounds sterling (GBP) and select “sender pays all charges” where your bank offers it, so the full rent reaches us. Transfers from overseas can take several working days — please allow for this so your rent arrives on time.

⚠️ Protect Yourself From Payment Fraud

We will never email, text or message you to say our bank details have changed. Criminals target tenants by impersonating landlords and sending fake “new bank details” messages. Money sent to a fraudster is very difficult to recover.

  • ›If you receive any message claiming our account has changed, do not pay it.
  • ›Check the details on this page against the details on your tenancy agreement.
  • ›If anything looks different, phone us on 01206 500202 before sending money. Use that number — not a number from the message.
  • ›Consider sending a small test payment first and confirming we have received it.
Home About Us

About Millennium

Family-run letting and property management across Essex, Suffolk, London and South Wales since 1998.

Our Story

Nearly Three Decades of Homes People Are Proud Of

Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd was founded in 1998 with a simple idea: that a rented home should feel like a real one. Nearly 28 years later, that principle still guides us — whether we're welcoming a first-year student into halls, handing over the keys to a young family in Colchester, or catching up with a long-term tenant we've known for years.

We're a family-run business. When you need us, you speak to someone who knows your property, your street, and often your name. It's an old-fashioned way of doing things, and we think that's what makes it work.

🏠 Applying & Viewing

You can apply by completing the online application form on our Private Rentals page, or by contacting us on 01206 500202 or enquiries@forestrd.co.uk. We will then arrange a viewing and walk you through the next steps.

Typically 3–7 working days once we have received all required documents and references. We'll keep you updated at every stage.

📋 Tenancy & Deposits

From 1 May 2026, following the Renters' Rights Act 2025, we issue Assured Periodic Tenancies (APTs) under the Housing Act 1988 (as amended). Assured Shorthold Tenancies (ASTs) and fixed-term tenancies have been abolished for both new and existing tenancies. Your tenancy will run on a rolling monthly basis with no fixed end date.

Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, all tenancies are now periodic (rolling) by law — there is no fixed term. The tenancy continues indefinitely until either party validly ends it: you can give two months' written notice at any time, and the landlord can only seek possession on prescribed statutory grounds. This gives tenants much more security and flexibility than under the old AST system.

No — our private rentals are offered on a no-deposit basis. You won't be asked for a tenancy deposit, holding deposit, application fee or referencing fee. The only money payable at the start of your tenancy is your first month's rent plus one month's rent paid in advance.

In place of a deposit, our security rests on: (a) thorough pre-tenancy referencing including identity, employment, income and credit checks; (b) your National Insurance number and date of birth held on file for tracing purposes; (c) your written consent (Schedule C of the tenancy agreement) to credit reference and tracing searches; (d) a documented arrears escalation protocol; and (e) the landlord's reserved right to pursue civil money claims in the County Court for any unpaid rent or damages.

As no deposit is held, there is nothing to refund or deduct from. After check-out, we inspect the property against the check-in inventory. If you have left the property in the condition expected (allowing for fair wear and tear) and have no rent or utility arrears, there is nothing further to do. If there is damage beyond fair wear and tear or unpaid sums, we will pursue this as a civil money claim in the County Court rather than withholding any deposit.

Break clauses are no longer relevant under the Renters' Rights Act 2025. Because all tenancies are now periodic (rolling), you can give two months' written notice to end the tenancy at any time — there is no fixed term to "break out of". This gives you greater flexibility than the previous fixed-term AST model.

💷 Rent, Bills & Council Tax

In most of our private rentals, bills are not included unless specifically stated. You'll be responsible for setting up and paying for gas, electricity, water, broadband, council tax and TV licence. We'll confirm which (if any) bills are included before you sign.

Rent is paid monthly in advance by standing order to our nominated account. Bank details are provided in your tenancy agreement.

Rent is due on the same date each month, as set out in your tenancy agreement — usually the date the tenancy began.

Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, rent can be increased no more than once per year, and only by serving a Section 13 notice. You will be given at least two months' written notice of any proposed increase. Pre-existing rent review clauses in your contract are overridden by statute and have no effect. You have the right to challenge any proposed increase at the First-tier Tribunal if you believe it exceeds market rent.

Yes. Council tax is the tenant's responsibility unless all occupants qualify for an exemption (e.g. full-time students). You will need to register with the local council when you move in.

Yes, if you watch or record live TV, or use BBC iPlayer. See www.tvlicensing.co.uk for further details.

🛠️ The Property & Repairs

Yes — under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, requests to keep a pet at the property are considered on their merits and cannot be unreasonably refused. The landlord may require you to maintain pet damage insurance, or pay a reasonable contribution towards such cover. Please let us know in writing as part of your application.

No, smoking is not permitted inside any of our properties. You are welcome to smoke outside, away from doors and windows.

Yes, occasional overnight guests are absolutely fine. However, only those named on the tenancy agreement may live at the property permanently. If your circumstances change, please contact us so we can update the agreement.

This depends on the property. Some have allocated off-street parking, some have permit street parking, and others have a driveway. We confirm exact parking arrangements for each property at the viewing.

Under Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, we (the landlord) are responsible for maintaining the structure, exterior, heating, water, gas and electrical installations. Tenants are responsible for taking reasonable care of the property and reporting issues promptly.

You can report issues by emailing enquiries@forestrd.co.uk, calling 01206 500202, or using the contact form on this website. Emergencies (major water leak, no heating in winter, no power, security risk) should always be reported by phone.

It depends on how serious the problem is. Genuine emergencies — loss of heating, water or power, or anything presenting a security or safety risk — are attended to as quickly as possible. Less urgent repairs are scheduled according to priority.

Repairs are carried out by our own in-house maintenance team, and we will keep you informed of timescales throughout.

Our buildings insurance covers the property itself, but not your personal belongings. We strongly recommend taking out tenants' contents insurance to protect your possessions.

Where the property has a private garden, day-to-day garden maintenance (mowing, weeding, keeping it tidy) is the tenant's responsibility. Structural matters such as fence repairs and major tree work are dealt with by us.

You may hang pictures using suitable picture hooks. Painting, wallpapering or any other decorative changes require our written permission in advance.

🔑 Moving In & Moving Out

Move-in dates are agreed when you sign the tenancy agreement and pay the first month's rent and deposit. We aim to make every property "move-in ready" — cleaned, with all appliances and utilities working.

We carry out a detailed inventory and schedule of condition at the start of the tenancy, including photos. You'll have 7 days to review the document and add any comments before it is finalised — this protects both parties at the end of the tenancy.

Yes. We may carry out periodic inspections (typically every 3–6 months) with at least 24 hours' written notice, as required by law. The purpose is to check for any issues that need attention before they become serious.

Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, you can end the tenancy at any time by giving at least two months' written notice to the landlord. The notice must be in writing and must expire at the end of a rental period. There is no longer a "fixed term" to commit to — you have flexibility from day one.

The property should be returned in the same condition as recorded on the check-in inventory, allowing for fair wear and tear. That includes a thorough clean, removal of all your belongings, and taking final meter readings on move-out day.

No, subletting is not permitted. Only those named on the tenancy agreement may live at the property.

Government Information Sheet — Renters' Rights Act 2025

By law, all tenants in the private rented sector must receive this sheet by 28 May 2026.

↓ View PDF
Important — Renters' Rights Act 2025 status. Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd has applied for membership of a Government-approved code of practice for student accommodation providers. Pending approval of this membership, certain provisions of the Renters' Rights Act 2025 — which came into force on 1 May 2026 — may apply to your tenancy alongside these terms. Once our code membership is confirmed, the full student-let exemption will apply and we will update these terms accordingly. The Government Information Sheet linked above sets out your rights in full.

Occupants

All occupants must be in full time education.

Bookings

Late bookings will be accepted, if places are available. Should the property you wish be full, then we will hold a first come first served waiting list.

Additional Charges

In the event that rent remains unpaid for a period of more than 14 days from the date on which the same is due, a fee will be charged which is equal to 3% above the Bank of England's base rate of the rental amount that is overdue. This fee will continue to accrue until the date on which payment is made.

All charges set out below comply with Schedule 1 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019 and represent reasonable costs incurred by the landlord.

Charge Fee
False Alarm Call-Out £25
Lock-Out Charge (Out of Office Hours) £10
Replacement Key Charge £10

Miscellaneous

Monthly room inspections will be carried out by the Landlord or his representatives.

Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd reserves the right to charge a payment in respect of damages for breach of the tenancy agreement, if it is so breached.

Please note that whilst network and internet services are available, the equipment and services belong to and are the responsibility of Glide — therefore any complaints, problems or issues must be taken up with Glide directly. Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd accept no responsibility or liability whatsoever from any issues which arise from or by the use of the service. Please contact them directly on 0333 123 0115. In the event of a dispute with the internet service, the liability of Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd is limited to the pro-rata rate it pays to the service provider.

Council Tax

Full-time students are exempt from paying council tax under the Local Government Finance Act 1992. To maintain this exemption, you must provide a valid Student Certificate issued by your university, which we will share with the local council where required. If at any time you cease to be a full-time student during your tenancy, you must notify us immediately, as the council tax liability will transfer to you.

Right to Rent

In accordance with the Immigration Act 2014, we are required by law to verify that all occupants have the right to live in the UK before the tenancy commences. You will be asked to provide original identification documents (e.g. passport, BRP or other approved ID) so we can complete this check in person. Copies of these documents are retained for the duration of your tenancy in compliance with Home Office requirements.

Updated for the Renters' Rights Act 2025. These terms reflect the new private rented sector regime that came into force on 1 May 2026, including the abolition of Assured Shorthold Tenancies and the move to Assured Periodic Tenancies.

Tenancy Type

The tenancy granted is an Assured Periodic Tenancy under the Housing Act 1988, as amended by the Renters' Rights Act 2025. The tenancy runs on a rolling monthly basis with no fixed end date. Existing Assured Shorthold Tenancies granted before 1 May 2026 were automatically converted to Assured Periodic Tenancies on that date.

Occupancy & Subletting

Only persons named on the tenancy agreement may occupy the property as their primary residence. Any change in occupancy must be agreed by the landlord in writing in advance. Subletting and lodging are not permitted under any circumstances.

Reservation (No Holding Deposit)

We do not require any holding deposit, application fee or reservation fee to apply for one of our properties. Reservation is confirmed in writing once your application has been received, referencing checks have been satisfactorily completed, and a mutually agreed move-in date has been set. The only monies payable at the start of your tenancy are your first month's rent and one further month's rent paid in advance, in accordance with section 4B of the Housing Act 1988 (as inserted by the Renters' Rights Act 2025).

No Deposit Tenancy

Our private rentals are offered on a no-deposit basis. No tenancy deposit is taken, requested or held under the tenancy agreement. This represents a significant cost saving for our tenants — typically £1,000+ that would otherwise be tied up for the duration of the tenancy.

In place of a deposit, our security rests on the following protections, which form part of the tenancy agreement:

  • Thorough pre-tenancy referencing, including identity, employment, income and credit checks
  • The tenant's date of birth and National Insurance number, held on file for tracing and civil debt enforcement purposes
  • The tenant's written consent to credit reference and tracing searches (see Schedule C of the tenancy agreement)
  • A documented arrears escalation protocol activating well before any statutory threshold
  • The landlord's reserved right to pursue civil money claims in the County Court for any unpaid rent or damages, independently of and in addition to any possession proceedings

End-of-tenancy financial claims (e.g. for damage beyond fair wear and tear or unpaid rent) will be pursued as civil money claims in the County Court rather than deducted from any deposit. Any County Court Judgment (CCJ) registered against a tenant remains on their credit record for six years.

Rent & Advance Payments

Rent is payable monthly in advance by standing order to the landlord's nominated account. In compliance with the Renters' Rights Act 2025, no rent may be demanded or accepted before the tenancy agreement is signed, and the maximum amount payable in advance during the tenancy is one month's rent (or 28 days' rent where the rental period is shorter).

Rent Increases

Rent may only be increased once in any 12-month period. The landlord must serve a Section 13 notice in the prescribed form, giving at least 2 months' notice of the proposed increase. The new rent must reflect market rent. The tenant has the right to challenge the increase by applying to the First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber) before the date the increase is due to take effect.

Late Payment Charge

In the event that rent remains unpaid for a period of more than 14 days from the date on which the same is due, interest will be charged at a rate equal to 3% above the Bank of England's base rate, calculated daily on the overdue amount until payment is received in full. This complies with Schedule 1, Section 4 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

Permitted Charges

All charges set out below comply with Schedule 1 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

Charge Fee
Lost / Replacement Key Reasonable cost
Change of Sharer (tenant request) £50 + VAT
Early Surrender (tenant request) At landlord discretion

We do not charge any administration, referencing, renewal, check-in, check-out, inventory or other fees prohibited under the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

Tenant Notice to End Tenancy

The tenant may end the tenancy at any time by giving the landlord at least 2 months' written notice, in accordance with section 8(1) of the Renters' Rights Act 2025. The notice must be in writing and must expire at the end of a rental period.

Landlord Possession

The landlord may only seek possession of the property by serving a notice under Section 8 of the Housing Act 1988 (as amended), relying on one or more of the statutory grounds set out in Schedule 2. Notice periods vary by ground (typically 4 months for mandatory grounds such as Ground 1A — landlord selling the property — which cannot be used in the first 12 months of a tenancy). Section 21 "no-fault" evictions were abolished by the Renters' Rights Act 2025 on 1 May 2026.

Pet Requests

Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, you have the right to request to keep a pet at the property. We will consider any pet request reasonably and respond in writing within a reasonable period. Consent may be made conditional (for example, on you taking out pet insurance or paying a reasonable additional security deposit where permitted by law). Consent must not be unreasonably refused.

Anti-Discrimination

In accordance with the Renters' Rights Act 2025, we do not discriminate against prospective or existing tenants on the basis of receipt of housing benefit or other welfare benefits, having children in the household, or other protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010.

Repairs, Maintenance & Inspections

In accordance with Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, the landlord is responsible for keeping in repair: (a) the structure and exterior of the property; (b) installations for the supply of water, gas and electricity, and for sanitation; (c) installations for space heating and water heating.

The tenant is responsible for: keeping the property in a clean and tenantable condition; replacing items such as light bulbs and fuses; and preventing damage by negligence, misuse or wilful act.

Reporting of defects: The tenant must report any disrepair, defect, damage or service failure to the landlord in writing within 48 hours of becoming aware of it. Where the tenant fails to report promptly and the defect worsens as a result, any consequential damage may be attributed to the tenant's failure to report.

Inspections: The landlord may carry out routine inspections of the property up to four times per year, on no less than 24 hours' written notice as required by law. Photographic records may be taken at each visit.

Insurance

Buildings insurance is maintained by the landlord. Tenants are strongly advised to take out tenants' contents insurance to protect their personal belongings, as these are not covered by the landlord's policy.

Smoking

The smoking of any substance — including tobacco, cannabis and electronic cigarettes / vapes — is strictly not permitted anywhere inside the property or any communal area. The use of candles, open flames, joss sticks, oil burners or similar items is also prohibited. Tenants must not store flammable substances beyond small quantities of standard domestic products.

Alterations

Painting, wallpapering or any other decorative changes to the property require the landlord's prior written consent. Tenants must not install or change any locks, security fittings, TV aerials, satellite equipment or any external fitting without the landlord's prior written consent. Pictures may be hung using suitable picture hooks. Any consent granted may be made conditional on reinstatement at the end of the tenancy at the tenant's cost.

Utilities & Council Tax

Unless specifically stated as included in the tenancy agreement, the tenant is responsible for setting up and paying all utilities (gas, electricity, water, broadband), council tax and TV licence for the duration of the tenancy.

End of Tenancy

At the end of the tenancy, the property must be returned in the same condition as recorded on the check-in inventory, allowing for fair wear and tear. This includes a thorough clean, removal of all personal belongings, and final meter readings on the move-out date.

PRS Database & Landlord Ombudsman

Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd will register with the Private Rented Sector Database and the PRS Landlord Ombudsman in accordance with the Renters' Rights Act 2025, on the dates these schemes become operational.

Privacy Policy

Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd

Last updated: 13 May 2026  ·  Effective from: 1 May 2026

This privacy policy explains how Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd ("we", "us", "our") collects, uses and protects your personal information when you apply for our accommodation, become our tenant, visit our website or contact us. It is written to comply with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018.

1. Who We Are (Data Controller)

Millennium Investments 2000 Ltd is the Data Controller responsible for your personal information.

Registered office: Forest Road House, Forest Road, Colchester, Essex CO4 3XA
Contact: enquiries@forestrd.co.uk  ·  01206 500202

2. What Information We Collect

The categories of personal data we collect depend on whether you are applying for student accommodation or a private rental.

All applicants and tenants:

  • ›Identity data: full legal name, date of birth, nationality
  • ›Contact data: email address, phone number, current and forwarding addresses
  • ›Identification documents: passport, BRP, driving licence (for Right to Rent checks under the Immigration Act 2014)
  • ›Emergency contact details (name and phone of next of kin or guardian)
  • ›Signature (collected on the application form and tenancy agreement)
  • ›Tenancy records: rent payments, repair reports, inspection records, correspondence

Student applicants — in addition:

  • ›University, course, year of study and student ID
  • ›CAS letter and/or Student Certificate

Private rental applicants — in addition:

  • ›Employment data: employer, job title, length of employment, annual income
  • ›Proof of income: payslips, employment contract or bank statements
  • ›National Insurance number — collected for credit referencing and for tracing in the event of unpaid rent or damages
  • ›Previous landlord reference details
  • ›Credit history information obtained from credit reference agencies with your consent

3. Why We Use It & Legal Basis

Under Article 6 of the UK GDPR, every use of your data must have a lawful basis. Our processing relies on the following:

Purpose Legal Basis
Processing your application & managing your tenancyContract (Art. 6(1)(b))
Right to Rent checks; gas / electrical / EPC compliance; HMRC reportingLegal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c))
Credit referencing & tracing (private rental)Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) — Schedule C of tenancy agreement
Preventing fraud, recovering rent and damages, enforcing the tenancyLegitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f))
Verifying student status with universityContract (Art. 6(1)(b)) and Consent
Marketing communications (where you have opted in)Consent (Art. 6(1)(a))

4. Who We Share It With

We will not sell your data. We share it only with the parties listed below, and only to the extent necessary:

  • ›Credit reference agencies (e.g. Experian, Equifax, TransUnion) — for referencing and credit history reports (private rentals, with consent)
  • ›Tracing agents and solicitors — for locating tenants who have vacated with monies outstanding
  • ›The County Court — for money claims and possession proceedings, including registering County Court Judgments (CCJs)
  • ›Local authorities — for council tax registration and HMO licensing compliance
  • ›The Home Office — for Right to Rent disclosures where required by law
  • ›HMRC and DWP — where required for tax reporting or universal credit verification
  • ›University of Essex (and other educational institutions) — for verifying student status, with your consent
  • ›Maintenance contractors — limited to the minimum needed to carry out repairs at your property
  • ›The PRS Landlord Ombudsman and PRS Database — once these become operational under the Renters' Rights Act 2025
  • ›Service providers — our email host, form processor (Web3Forms), website host (GitHub Pages), all subject to written data processing agreements

5. How Long We Keep It

We only keep your information for as long as we need it for the purposes set out above, or as required by law:

  • ›Unsuccessful applications: 6 months from rejection (then securely deleted)
  • ›Tenancy records: 6 years from the end of the tenancy (the limitation period for contract and debt claims under the Limitation Act 1980)
  • ›Right to Rent records: throughout the tenancy plus 1 year afterwards, as required by the Home Office
  • ›Financial / accounting records: 6 years from the relevant tax year, as required by HMRC
  • ›Credit referencing records: 6 years (in line with the credit industry standard)
  • ›Marketing consents: until you withdraw consent or 3 years of inactivity
  • ›Website logs and cookies: 12 months maximum

6. International Transfers

Your data is processed and stored within the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area (EEA) where adequacy decisions apply. Some of our service providers (e.g. cloud email, form submission services) may process data on servers located in countries with appropriate UK GDPR safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses or adequacy decisions). We do not transfer your data to any country without such safeguards in place.

7. Your Rights

Under the UK GDPR you have the following rights, free of charge in most cases:

  • ›Access (Art. 15) — request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
  • ›Rectification (Art. 16) — ask us to correct any inaccurate or incomplete data
  • ›Erasure (Art. 17) — ask us to delete your data, subject to any legal retention requirements
  • ›Restriction (Art. 18) — ask us to stop processing your data in certain circumstances
  • ›Portability (Art. 20) — ask us to provide your data in a machine-readable format
  • ›Object (Art. 21) — object to processing based on legitimate interests, including direct marketing
  • ›Withdraw consent at any time, where processing is based on consent

To exercise any of these rights, please contact us. We will respond within one calendar month.

8. How to Complain — The ICO

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your personal data, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO):

Website: ico.org.uk
Phone: 0303 123 1113
Post: Information Commissioner's Office, Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire SK9 5AF

We would, however, appreciate the chance to deal with your concerns first — please contact us before approaching the ICO.

9. How We Protect Your Information

  • ›Personal data is stored on secure systems with access limited to authorised staff
  • ›All web traffic to this site is encrypted via HTTPS / TLS
  • ›Application form submissions are transmitted via an encrypted form service (Web3Forms)
  • ›We never ask for credit card or bank login details through our website
  • ›Documents containing sensitive data are securely shredded or digitally erased once retention periods expire

10. Cookies

Our website uses a minimal set of cookies and similar technologies:

  • ›Essential cookies — strictly necessary for the website to function (no consent required)
  • ›Local storage — to remember UI preferences (e.g. signed reviews, dismissed banners) within your browser only

We do not use third-party advertising or tracking cookies. You can disable cookies in your browser at any time without affecting the core functionality of the site.

11. Changes to This Policy

We may update this privacy policy from time to time, particularly to reflect legal changes or new processing activities. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page will always reflect the most recent revision. For material changes, we will give existing tenants reasonable advance notice.

12. Contact Us

If you have any questions about this policy or how we handle your data, please contact us:
